name: Siege of Alesia
intro: The hill-town of Alesia in Burgundy, in September. You are Julius Caesar, with 10 or 11 legions and auxiliaries, perhaps 60,000 to 75,000 men. Vercingetorix is inside the town with about 80,000. A Gallic relief army is coming: Caesar says 250,000, modern historians say 50,000 to 100,000.
debrief: In reality, Caesar surrounded Alesia with two rings of works: one facing the town, about 16 km long, and one facing outward, about 21 km, with ditches, towers and fields of sharpened stakes and pits. His Germanic cavalry beat the Gallic horse. Vercingetorix sent the old, the sick and the women and children of the town out between the lines; Caesar refused to let them through and they starved. The relief army attacked by day and by night; Antony and Trebonius brought troops from distant forts. At noon on the last day Vercassivellaunus attacked the weak northern camp with 60,000 men. Labienus held it with fresh cohorts, Caesar arrived with more, and cavalry rode out behind the Gauls. The relief army broke, and Vercingetorix surrendered. Casualty figures are uncertain and Caesar’s are thought exaggerated. The northern camp sat on awkward ground because the hill above it was too large to bring inside the lines; enclosing it, like the other choices, is a what-if.

win: The cavalry bursts out behind the Gauls.
lose: Caesar is trapped between two armies.

decisions.title: Trapping Vercingetorix
decisions.text: Vercingetorix has shut himself and about 80,000 men in the hill-town of Alesia. A great relief army is being raised across Gaul.

hint.text: The hill is too strong to storm. Help is coming for the Gauls.

scout.text: A ring of works facing the town traps the Gauls. A second ring facing outward protects you from the relief army. It is enormous labour, but it makes your army a fortress.

choices.label: Build two rings of works, inner and outer

fx.text: Your legions dig two lines of ditches, ramparts and towers, the inner one about 16 km and the outer about 21 km around, sown with sharpened stakes and hidden pits. One camp in the north is left on steep, awkward ground: the hill above it is too big to bring inside the lines.

choices.label: Storm the hill at once, before the relief army can gather

fx.text: The legions are hurled back from the slopes.

choices.label: Build both rings, wide enough to take in the north hill

fx.text: The rings are longer and the men dig for weeks more, but the northern hill is inside your works. There is no weak camp.

decisions.title: The cavalry fight
decisions.text: Gallic cavalry rides out to stop the digging. The plain between the lines is open ground.

hint.text: Your Germanic horsemen are eager to fight.

scout.text: Your German cavalry are better than the Gauls’ in a hard fight. Unleashed now, they can break the Gallic horse and protect the work.

choices.label: Send the German cavalry at them

fx.text: The Germanic horse crashes into the Gauls and drives them back to the town gates.

choices.label: Pull the workers back behind the ditches

fx.text: The work stops while the Gauls ride about.

choices.label: Send the legions out onto the plain

fx.text: The Gallic horse rides rings round them.

decisions.title: The night attack
decisions.text: The relief army has arrived. At night it attacks your outer line, while Vercingetorix attacks the inner one.

hint.text: The attack is hitting a sector far from your nearest troops.

scout.text: Your officers in the quiet sectors can bring cohorts from distant forts to wherever the line is pressed.

choices.label: Bring troops over from the distant forts

fx.text: The stakes and pits break up the night attack. Antony and Trebonius bring men from distant forts. At dawn the relief army pulls back.

choices.label: Hold every man in his own sector so no gap opens

fx.text: The pressed sectors are short of men.

choices.label: Sally out against the relief army

fx.text: In the dark your men run onto their own traps.

decisions.title: The weak camp
decisions.text: At noon Vercassivellaunus leads 60,000 picked men against your weakest point: a camp in the north, on steep, awkward ground, held by two legions. Vercingetorix attacks the inner line at the same time.

hint.text: The northern camp is on bad ground and is giving way.

scout.text: Your best lieutenant, with fresh cohorts and orders to hold, can steady the northern camp until you bring up more.

choices.label: Send Labienus with six cohorts to hold it

fx.text: With the hill inside your works, Vercassivellaunus’s men attack a strong rampart from below. Labienus throws them back.
Labienus holds the northern camp, just. The Gauls are spent from the night before.

choices.label: Strip the inner line to save the camp

fx.text: The camp holds, but Vercingetorix nearly breaks out.

choices.label: Let the camp fall and form a new line behind

decisions.title: Caesar’s cloak
decisions.text: Labienus can barely hold. You have fresh cohorts and the cavalry in hand. The Gauls can see your general’s scarlet cloak if you ride forward.

hint.text: The relief army has committed almost everything to this attack.

scout.text: If Caesar arrives with fresh cohorts while the cavalry rides out through the outer line to strike the relief army from behind, the attack breaks.

choices.label: Ride to the camp yourself, cavalry round behind

fx.text: Caesar arrives in his cloak with fresh cohorts, and the cavalry bursts out behind the Gauls. The relief army flees. In Alesia, Vercingetorix lays down his arms.

choices.label: Send the reserves forward, but stay at the centre to direct

fx.text: The attack is held, but not broken.
The cavalry is too few on its own.
